## Analysis Summary

**Test image observations:**
- Sugarcane leaf, mostly green and healthy-looking
- **One prominent white/pale stripe** running longitudinally along the leaf blade
- No mosaicing, no discrete spots, no general yellowing

**Reference image comparisons:**
1. **Streak_Mosaic_Scsmv**: Shows multiple very fine, subtle yellow-green streaks distributed throughout — does NOT match the single bold stripe in the test image
2. **Leaf_Scald**: Shows a single prominent white/pale scald stripe running along the leaf on green background — **strong visual match** with the test image
3. **Yellow_Leaf**: Shows entirely yellowed/cream-colored leaf tissue — clearly not a match
4. (Budget used across 4 different classes)

The single prominent white/pale longitudinal stripe on an otherwise green leaf is the hallmark of **Leaf Scald** disease (*Xanthomonas albilineans*), which produces characteristic white "pencil-line" or broader pale stripes running parallel to leaf veins. This directly matches the Leaf_Scald reference image.
